root_cause.text: The use of mutable scalar fields (x->km.seq and x->id.spi) as predicates for hash list removal in __xfrm_state_delete, combined with the lack of idempotent deletion for bydst/bysrc, allows a second deletion to attempt to unhash an already-removed node, causing a use-after-free write through LIST_POISON pprev.
root_cause.evidence: The patch description states: "__xfrm_state_delete() guards its byseq and byspi unhashes with value-based predicates: if (x->km.seq) hlist_del_rcu(&x->byseq); if (x->id.spi) hlist_del_rcu(&x->byspi);" and "the bydst/bysrc unhashes have no predicate at all, so a second __xfrm_state_delete() on the same object writes through LIST_POISON pprev." The fix changes these to use `hlist_unhashed()` and `hlist_del_init_rcu()` to ensure safe double-deletion.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential list corruption and use-after-free by reinitializing hlist nodes after deletion and using proper hash status checks before removal.
intent_record.what: In __xfrm_state_delete, replaced hlist_del_rcu with hlist_del_init_rcu for bydst, bysrc, byseq, byspi lists; changed deletion condition for byseq from 'x->km.seq' to '!hlist_unhashed(&x->byseq)', and for byspi from 'x->id.spi' to '!hlist_unhashed(&x->byspi)'.
